headline: Former police officer arrested after 6 years on the run only because he forgot to update his Zomato delivery address
body:
"I honestly thought he was just a retired gym teacher who really liked extra-spicy paneer rolls every Tuesday night," said local food delivery rider Ravi Kumar, who noticed the suspect's 'Wanted' poster while waiting for an order at the front gate.

"He was always so polite when I handed him his food, but he never took off his sunglasses or his full-face motorbike helmet, which I assumed was just a fashion choice for the suburban lifestyle," noted neighborhood shopkeeper Mrs. Deshmukh.

"I tried to tell him that using a fake name on a food app is fine, but you really shouldn't use your own personal fingerprint for the 'one-tap login' feature if you're trying to stay hidden from the entire state police force," shared software engineering student Arjun Mehta.

"It’s honestly a bit embarrassing for the whole department that it took a customer feedback notification about a missing side of extra chutney to finally pinpoint his location after half a decade of high-level surveillance," remarked a local traffic constable who requested anonymity.

"If he had just switched to an office address for his deliveries instead of using his secret hideout, he probably could have kept his freedom for another ten years, at least," sighed a resident of the housing colony.
caption: The most professional criminal career in history has come to an end over a missing order of extra chutney. Sometimes, the real enemy isn't the law, it's the lack of side dishes. #Zomato #CrimeStories #Fail (satire)
igHook: Would you risk being caught by the police just to get your favorite late-night snack delivered?
imagePrompt: A generic, slightly blurry photo of a residential building entrance with a discarded paper food delivery bag sitting on the concrete steps.

sourceHeadline.title: Absconding ex-AIG Rajjit Singh arrested after nearly six years on the run

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 1 uses a specific, modern, and relatable absurdity—a Zomato delivery error—to ground the surreal premise of a six-year fugitive. It avoids the repetitive 'hide-and-seek' trope seen in many other candidates and uses specific, non-formulaic details (like the 'one-tap login' fingerprint and extra chutney) to anchor the joke. It maintains a deadpan tone throughout, whereas other candidates leaned too heavily on self-explanatory jokes about the fugitives' incompetence.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article is a fictional, humorous piece about a hypothetical criminal. It uses generic names that do not identify specific private individuals, and the image prompt describes a generic scene without real-world identifying marks.
